messages:
claire: heads-up — AstraPath flagged INV-2026-0919: they were billed a burst overage despite having committed capacity for the same AZ. CSM wants a fix + customer note.
tom: can you paste the invoice lines and meter reference?
claire: pasted (trimmed):
```
line_id,nodepool,role,period_start,period_end,gpu_hours,unit_rate,discount_flag
L-70011,np-az1,dedicated-commit,2026-09-14T02:00Z,2026-09-14T03:00Z,12.0,2.00,false
L-70012,np-shared,shared-discount,2026-09-14T02:00Z,2026-09-14T03:00Z,12.0,2.00,true
L-70013,burst-overage,az1,2026-09-14T02:10Z,2026-09-14T02:40Z,3.0,3.50,false
```
billing-bot: Metering file uploaded: s3://exports/astrapath/2026-09/meter-0914.csv md5: ff12b6.
rachel (CS): customer says they explicitly purchased two dedicated commits in az1; they saw the discount applied to a shared pool tag and were charged the burst. They're understandably upset.
nate (eng): quick root cause note: last-week pricing experiment enabled an optimization that applies "commit-discount" by tag map. a recent tag-normalizer change introduced a regression where dedicated pools with tag "commit:d-<id>" lost their canonical tag before billing; the discount matched a generic "shared" tag and not the dedicated pool. result: their reserved commit didn't get matched in aggregation, so we billed burst usage.
tom: numbers: burst 3.0 gpu-hours at $3.50 = $10.50 overage. customer also lost expected discount on 12 gpu-hours at $2.00 = $24.00 discount missing (12*$2.00*discount_rate?). need to be precise on what to credit.
claire: meter shows the dedicated pool consumed and should have been covered by commit. the easiest fix for customer is: 1) credit the burst $10.50 2) retroactively apply the committed discount differential: their invoice shows discount applied to shared pool instead — we should move the discount to their dedicated lines and issue net credit of $24.00 (estimated). total provisional credit = $34.50.
accounting-bot: Policy: provisional credits under $100 can be applied by billing ops with CSM approval. GL code: CUSTOMER_BILLING_ADJUSTMENTS.
Rachel: approved to apply provisional credit CR-2026-555 for $34.50 and send a transparent note: "pricing experiment regression caused commit-discount misattribution; provisional credit applied; engineering fix and post-mortem in progress." I'll send.
tom: also want to offer a small SLA goodwill: customer reported 12 minutes of increased error rate during the tagging rollout. Contract SLAs: >10m outage => prorated credit. propose SLA credit of $15.00 as goodwill and to preserve relationship. Approve?
rachel: approve — include SLA credit on same CR or separate? customer prefers single line on explanation.
accounting-bot: We prefer separate entries but can reference both in customer note. Create CR-2026-555 (billing adj) and CR-2026-556 (SLA credit $15.00).
nate: engineering action: rollback pricing experiment flag for tag-normalizer, add a defensive check in billing pipeline to prefer pool UUID match over fuzzy tag match, and add a nightly audit that ensures discounts are applied only to matching UUIDs. ETA: rollback + hotfix in 24h; audit in 72h. I'll open ENG-INC-3621.
claire: created FIN ticket FIN-2026-518 to track credits and audit. applied provisional CR-2026-555 ($34.50) and CR-2026-556 ($15.00) to INV-2026-0919. Accounting notified.
tom: send recovery note to product: this originated from a pricing experiment — need a post-mortem and stricter rollout checklist.
rachel: customer acknowledged receipt and said they appreciated the fast remediation. asked for the post-mortem when available. I'll loop them in once ENG-INC-3621 closes.
claire: next steps: engineering rollback + audit, finance to keep these provisional credits open until audit confirms numbers, CS to send customer post-mortem link when ready. closing day-of-thread after rollback confirmation. :white_check_mark:
